title: Unemployment rate jumps to 4.9% – the highest level in five years
summary:
Jobless rate rises from 4.7% to 4.9% for October, latest bureau of statistics figures reveal

Unemployment has surged to 4.9% in October, from 4.7%, in a shock increase that will add to…

blocks.text: Unemployment has surged to 4.9% in October, from 4.7%, in a shock increase that will add to rising worries the economy has passed a tipping point following this year’s five interest rate increases.
New figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the number of employed people dropped by 43,500 in the month, confounding forecasts for jobs growth and a steady jobless rate.
After starting the year at 4%, unemployment has now lifted to its highest level in five years to approach pre-Covid levels.

The shock figures will validate warnings from the three dissenting Reserve Bank of Australia board members, who voted against the Melbourne Cup day rate hike and warned of a “materially sharper downturn” in the economy as households struggled to deal with this year’s substantial lift in borrowing costs.
Full-time employment dropped by 2,900 in October, the ABS data showed, and part-time employment by a steeper 40,600 people.
